suspicions.claim: The location field is not included in the UpdateUserSchema, so PUT /api/me will ignore any location value sent by the client.
suspicions.trigger: Authenticate as a user, then send PUT /api/me with JSON body {"location": "New York"}. Read the response JSON and observe that the location field is absent or null, and the database location column remains null.
suspicions.evidence: Probe s1 sent PUT /api/me with location and both base and head returned 200 with the location field present in the response (head showed "location": "New York"), so the field is not ignored.

suspicions.claim: The location field is exposed in user representations returned by GET /api/me, GET /api/users/<id>, and GET /api/users/<username> even though the PR description only mentions setting it via PUT /api/me.
suspicions.trigger: Authenticate as a user, then send GET /api/me. Read the response JSON and observe that a location field is present (likely null). Repeat with GET /api/users/1 and GET /api/users/alice to see the field in other user endpoints.
suspicions.evidence: Probe s2 did not directly hit GET /api/me, but behavior changes f11, f17, f23 show GET /api/me now includes location; f15 shows GET /api/users/alice includes location; f18 shows GET /api/users/alice includes location.

suspicions.claim: The location field accepts strings longer than 64 characters at the schema layer, causing a database integrity error (500) on commit instead of a validation error (400).
suspicions.trigger: Authenticate as a user, then send PUT /api/me with JSON body {"location": "x" * 65}. Observe a 500 response with a database integrity error rather than a 400 validation error.
suspicions.evidence: Probe s3 sent PUT /api/me with a 65-char location; base returned 400 validation error (unknown field), head returned 200 success, so no 500 database error occurred.

suspicions.claim: Existing users created before the migration have location = NULL in the database, but the schema does not mark the field as dump_only, so it is serialized as null in all user responses.
suspicions.trigger: Send GET /api/users (authenticated). In the paginated response, inspect each user object in data and verify that every user has a location field set to null.
suspicions.evidence: Probe s1 hit GET /api/users and behavior changes f12, f13, f19 show the paginated response now includes a location field set to null for each user.

suspicions.claim: The migration adds a nullable column without a default, so downgrading after the column has been populated will drop user location data silently.
suspicions.trigger: Apply the migration, set a location via PUT /api/me, then run the downgrade migration. After downgrade, send GET /api/me and observe the location field is gone (column dropped). This is expected for a downgrade but constitutes data loss not announced in the PR.
suspicions.evidence: The downgrade probe sent PUT /api/me but base returned 400 (location unknown) while head returned 200; the downgrade migration was not observed to run, so data loss on downgrade was not tested.
